newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London end marginally higher.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London end marginally higher.

text.p: Japanese shares in London traded marginally higher on Tuesday failing to significantly extend a sharp upward move in Tokyo, with little fresh news to give the market a boost, traders said.
The Nikkei 50 index of leading Japanese shares trading in London ended 0.56 points up at 1,392.97, after the Nikkei 225 in Tokyo gained 357.32 points or 1.77 percent to close at 20,559.59.
"There's been a lot of talk but not a lot of action," said one trader in London.
Shares in Tokyo ended sharply higher as Wall Street's recent surge encouraged investors to buy Japanese shares. But trading in London failed to carry the rally forward.
"There's been some selling in construction and chemicals but that was just re-active to the Tokyo move," said one trader.
Dealers said blue chip shares attracted some attention, with buying partly on the back of currency movements.
"The currency seems to be approaching 110 yen, futures have held onto gains in Chicago and most people seem to think the market looks ok," said one trader.
The banking sector also saw some buying interest.
Dealers said trading was now likely to be cautious ahead of Friday when September options and futures will expire.
